brief: Havora's mountain (town/ground.js '^' and its upper tier 'M') read as a flat grey field of cobble/flagstone plates with boulders on it (Coordinator, seams-2 audit). Wanted: real rock, cliff faces lit from the upper left, scree at the foot, grass tufts in the cracks, organic edges.
call: create_topdown_tileset mode pro, 32 px, high top-down, lower 'light tan packed dirt road' (not used: the town's own dirt and grass are the floors), palette = hr-world-56-v2 stone, shadow, moss (and leaf, earth) ramps, max_colors 10-12; no chained base (the 11-11 palette lesson). Imported as drawn: every opaque pixel a palette entry (havora-seams.mjs sheetCut checks it).

r1-181b4f19.verdict: REFUSED: drew crazy paving (polygon slabs with joints), the look the brief was written against

wiring: tools/world-art/havora-seams.mjs: the slopes ('^') take r5's fill as drawn, the upper terraces ('M') the same fill a value step up; every rock pair (grass, dirt, the quarry's gravel, the sea, and rock/peak) draws its south edges with r5's face rows and its sides with a 4 px strip of them (seams.mjs rise faceTex, side). The cliff and peak varieties shift the grain inside the tile and add pebbles and grass tufts.
